task: Owner request: run the IDP portal in the local Vagrant cluster as a DEV build with live editing. The documented skaffold path was broken: portal/deploy/skaffold-dev-portal.yaml was a stale hand copy of the chart Deployment (missing Valkey creds, token volumes, securityContext) that ArgoCD selfHeal would revert, skaffold.yaml pointed at a deleted ../narwhal path, ignoreDifferences covered only image/resources, and the chart 512Mi limit OOMs next dev. Generate the dev Deployment from the chart at run time and change only image, resources and a startupProbe. No cluster is available; live verification is listed, not claimed.

events.summary: Replace the hand-kept dev manifest with portal/scripts/dev-cluster.sh, which renders the chart Deployment as ArgoCD does (narwhal-apps valuesObject for narwhal-platform -> helm template narwhal-platform) and changes exactly container narwhal-portal image (harbor dev repo, skaffold tags it dev-*), resources (requests memory 1Gi, limits cpu 1 / memory 3Gi) and startupProbe (/api/health/live, 5s x 60). Ignore fields owned by field manager narwhal-portal-dev in argocd-cm (D-PORTAL-DEV-FIELD-MANAGER, replacing the first-draft :dev- jq guard), repoint skaffold.yaml, delete the stale copy, add make dev-cluster / pnpm dev:cluster, update the live-dev docs, add R299 and a lessons-log row. Deliberately left alone: the Valkey Deployment, Service, secrets and RBAC (ArgoCD-managed, never applied by skaffold), the debug profile's kaniko build, the other ignoreDifferences entries, and any live cluster.

On origin/main the dev manifest differs from the chart: diffing portal/deploy/skaffold-dev-portal.yaml against the helm-rendered Deployment shows no VALKEY_USERNAME/VALKEY_PASSWORD, K8S_SA_TOKEN_FILE, openbao-token or k8s-api-token volumes and no pod/container securityContext; portal/skaffold.yaml:54 references ../narwhal/gitops/resources/narwhal-portal-k8s.yaml which does not exist in the monorepo; argocd-config.yaml ignores only .image and .resources.

dev-cluster.sh --render-only emits only Deployment narwhal-portal; diff against the chart render shows exactly image, resources and the added startupProbe. The script refuses a kube context other than narwhal and a baseDomain other than local.narwhal.internal, patches the live argocd-cm apps_Deployment key when it differs from the chart (the ConfigMap self-ignore means git edits never reach a running cluster), probes Harbor TLS and adds skaffold --insecure-registry only when system trust fails, and --restore (also an EXIT/INT trap) re-applies the git Deployment as argocd-controller, releases narwhal-portal-dev with an empty apply, and requests an ArgoCD refresh. argocd-config.yaml apps_Deployment is exactly managedFieldsManagers: [narwhal-portal-dev]; skaffold's dev deploy applies with --server-side --force-conflicts --field-manager=narwhal-portal-dev.

The first mutation set had a no-op mutation (deleting the pod securityContext inside the container-scoped yq update did nothing); R299 mutation verification reported it as surviving, so it was replaced by a pod-level delete after the container update plus a container-level delete. All 7 mutations are now caught. Second correction from the live test on the local cluster (2026-11-02): ArgoCD v3.4.4 applies jqPathExpressions to both target and live, so the first-draft select(.image | test(":dev-")) guard matched nothing on the git target (image 1.1.5) but removed .image/.resources/.startupProbe from live; the permanent asymmetric diff made selfHeal revert the dev Deployment within about 1-30 s (reproduced twice). The argocd-cm ConfigMap self-ignore also hides edits to that key from existing clusters. A jq-free managedFieldsManagers: [narwhal-portal-dev] plus a server-side apply as that manager held the image 90 s+ with the app Synced. skaffold's digest lookup on the Mac failed x509 against a stale keychain CA although docker push worked; --insecure-registry fixed it. Live testing then showed the jq-guard ignore was asymmetric and selfHeal reverted the dev Deployment; the design moved to managedFieldsManagers (D-PORTAL-DEV-FIELD-MANAGER) with an argocd-cm hot-patch preflight, a Harbor TLS fallback and a restore trap. Independent review of 28eb024b (native Sonnet) then found this trace still described the pre-live state (no cluster, 7 mutations) and that restore() did not stop after a failed first apply; both corrected.
evidence: test:live 2026-11-02 on the local cluster by the coordinator: jq-guard variant reverted within 1-30 s (x2); managedFieldsManagers variant held image 90 s+, app Synced

events.scope: static: chart render diff, R299 with 10 mutations, full static suite, trace validators. LIVE on the local cluster (box 0.3.1, 2026-11-02): ArgoCD non-revert, HMR, restore. NOT covered: the argocd-cm hot-patch WITHOUT an application-controller restart (in the manual field-manager test the controller was restarted after patching; in the scripted end-to-end run the live key already matched the chart, so no patch happened), browser SSO login against the dev pod, a 3Gi dev pod on a 2-vCPU worker.
evidence: runtime:jq-guard design (706d13ca) on the live cluster: ArgoCD v3.4.4 self-healed the dev Deployment back to 1.1.5 within ~30 s (op 2026-11-02T00:29:55Z) - asymmetric normalization of select(.image|test(':dev-'))

runtime:KUBE_CONTEXT=narwhal bash portal/scripts/dev-cluster.sh -> Harbor TLS probe warned and added --insecure-registry (macOS keychain held an older cluster CA), build+push+deploy, 'Deployments stabilized', dev image held 120 s, narwhal-platform Synced, ready 1/1

runtime:edit src/app/api/health/live/route.ts (add hmrProbe) -> skaffold 'Syncing 1 files', https://portal.local.narwhal.internal/api/health/live returned hmrProbe within 2 s, pid unchanged (37), restartCount 0; revert removed it

events.summary: On the local cluster a dev portal generated from the chart stays deployed under ArgoCD selfHeal, file saves reach it by HMR within seconds, and exiting hands the Deployment back to argocd-controller at the git image.
Complete and verified live for the API path; browser SSO against the dev pod and the no-restart hot-patch path remain unverified.
